cmd.root.short: Portable authenticator with tamper-evident audit logging
cmd.root.long:
Tegata is a portable authenticator that stores encrypted credentials
on USB drives or microSD cards with optional tamper-evident audit logging
via ScalarDL Ledger.
cmd.root.example:
tegata version          Show version information
  tegata code GitHub     Generate TOTP code for GitHub
  tegata --verbose code  Generate code with debug logging
cmd.root.flag.vault: path to vault file or directory
cmd.root.flag.lang: language for this invocation (en-us, ja-jp); use tegata config set language to persist
cmd.ui.long:
Launch the interactive terminal user interface for Tegata.

If no vault is found, the first-time setup wizard guides you through vault
creation. If a vault exists, you will be prompted to unlock it.
cmd.ui.flag.vault: Path to vault file or directory

cmd.export.short: Export all credentials to an encrypted backup file
cmd.export.long:
Export encrypts all credentials in the vault to a portable .tegata-backup file.
The backup is protected by a new export passphrase that you choose — it is
independent of your vault passphrase. Anyone who has the backup file and its
passphrase can restore your credentials.
cmd.export.flag.out: output path for the backup file (default: vault.tegata-backup in vault directory)
cmd.export.flag.vault: path to vault file or directory
cmd.export.info.choosePass: Choose a passphrase for the backup file (separate from your vault passphrase).
cmd.export.error.shortPass: Error: export passphrase must be at least 8 characters.
cmd.export.error.passMismatch: Error: passphrases do not match. Try again.
cmd.get.example:
tegata get backup-key
  tegata get --show backup-key
cmd.history.short: View authentication history from ScalarDL Ledger
cmd.history.long:
Retrieve and display authentication event records from the ScalarDL Ledger.
Events are stored as hashed records; label and service name hashes protect
user privacy in the audit log.

Requires audit to be enabled in tegata.toml ([audit] enabled = true).
cmd.history.example:
tegata history
  tegata history --from 2026-01-01 --to 2026-03-31
  tegata history --type totp
  tegata history --sort operation --order asc
  tegata history --limit 20
  tegata history --json
cmd.history.flag.type: filter by operation type (e.g., totp, hotp, vault-unlock)
cmd.history.flag.sort: sort column (operation, label, timestamp, hash); default: timestamp
cmd.history.flag.order: sort order (asc, desc); default: desc when --sort is timestamp, asc otherwise
cmd.history.flag.limit: maximum number of rows to display (0 = no limit)
cmd.history.error.invalidSort: invalid --sort value {{.Value}} (expected: operation, label, timestamp, hash): {{.Err}}
cmd.import.short: Import credentials from an encrypted backup file
cmd.import.long:
Import restores credentials from a .tegata-backup file into the current vault.
Credentials whose label already exists in the vault are skipped.
You will be prompted for the backup passphrase (the one set during export).

For scripted restore flows the backup passphrase may be supplied via the
TEGATA_BACKUP_PASSPHRASE environment variable. This variable is intentionally
separate from TEGATA_PASSPHRASE (the vault passphrase). Export never reads
this variable — an interactive prompt is always required to set a new backup
passphrase — so the variable is safe to set in restore automation without
risking accidental export with a known passphrase.
cmd.import.flag.vault: path to vault file or directory
cmd.import.error.fileTooLarge: backup file too large ({{.Size}} bytes, max {{.Max}})

cmd.ledger.long:
Commands for configuring and verifying the optional ScalarDL Ledger
audit integration. The audit layer records authentication events in a
tamper-evident ledger for post-hoc integrity verification.
cmd.ledger.setup.short: Register HMAC secret and verify connectivity
cmd.ledger.setup.long:
Register the HMAC secret key with the ScalarDL Ledger privileged
service and verify that the ledger is reachable.

This command must be run once before audit logging is active. It reads the
[audit] section from tegata.toml (located in the vault directory) and uses
the configured secret key and server address.

To configure tegata.toml for a local ScalarDL instance:

[audit]
server = "127.0.0.1:50051"
privileged_server = "127.0.0.1:50052"
entity_id = "tegata-client"
key_version = 1
insecure = true

For a remote instance with TLS, omit insecure (or set it to false). Run
'tegata ledger start' for automatic Docker-based setup instead.
cmd.ledger.setup.example:
tegata ledger setup
  tegata ledger setup --vault /media/usb
cmd.ledger.start.long:
Start the ScalarDL Ledger Docker stack and configure audit logging.

This command:
  1. Checks Docker is installed
  2. Extracts the bundled docker-compose.yml to ~/.tegata/docker/
  3. Generates an entity ID and secret key from your vault
  4. Starts the Docker stack (docker compose up -d)
  5. Waits for the ledger to become ready (up to 30 seconds)
  6. Registers audit credentials with the ledger
  7. Writes the [audit] section to tegata.toml

After running this command, audit logging is active immediately. Subsequent
vault unlocks auto-start the Docker stack if it is not already running.
cmd.ledger.start.example:
tegata ledger start
  tegata ledger start --vault /media/usb
cmd.ledger.stop.short: Stop the ledger server Docker containers
cmd.ledger.stop.long:
Stop the ScalarDL Ledger Docker containers.

Containers are stopped and your audit history is preserved
(docker compose stop, named volume retained).
cmd.ledger.stop.example:
tegata ledger stop
  tegata ledger stop --vault /media/usb

cmd.verify.short: Verify hash-chain integrity of the audit log
cmd.verify.long:
Call the ScalarDL Ledger to verify the integrity of all audit records.
Reports the number of events checked and whether the hash chain is intact.

Exits with code 0 on success, code 9 on integrity violation, or code 8 on
network failure.

Requires audit to be enabled in tegata.toml ([audit] enabled = true).
